title: Accepted Identity Documents and Document Limits Under Claimant Identity Verification
content:
For Claimant Identity Verification, the identity documents a claimant must present, the forms in which they are taken and the limits on rejected documents are set per proofing pathway as follows.

## A. Number of documents and accepted form

| Pathway | Primary photo documents required | Secondary documents required in addition | Form in which documents are accepted |
|---|---|---|---|
| Online Identity Proofing (IAL2) | 1 | 0 | uploaded image |
| Video Trusted Referee Session | 1 | 0 | uploaded image |
| In-Person Proofing — American Job Center | 1 | 1 | original |
| In-Person Proofing — USPS Retail Location | 1 | 0 | original |
| Documentary Verification by Mail | 1 | 1 | photocopy |
| Identity Theft Victim Re-Verification | 1 | 1 | original |

## B. Accepted primary photo documents

- **Online Identity Proofing (IAL2):** state driver's license; state ID card; U.S. passport.
- **Video Trusted Referee Session:** state driver's license; state ID card; U.S. passport; permanent resident card.
- **In-Person Proofing — American Job Center, In-Person Proofing — USPS Retail Location, Documentary Verification by Mail and Identity Theft Victim Re-Verification:** state driver's license; state ID card; U.S. passport; permanent resident card; military ID.

## C. Accepted secondary documents

- **In-Person Proofing — American Job Center** and **Documentary Verification by Mail:** Social Security card; Form W-2; birth certificate; DD Form 214; federal Standard Form 50 (SF-50).
- **Identity Theft Victim Re-Verification:** Social Security card; Form W-2; birth certificate.
- **Online Identity Proofing (IAL2), Video Trusted Referee Session** and **In-Person Proofing — USPS Retail Location:** none (no secondary document is required).

## D. Expired documents, name differences, resubmission and authenticity

| Pathway | Months after expiration an expired primary document is still accepted | Legal name-change document required when a document name differs from the profile | Times a rejected document of the same role may be resubmitted | Document failing authenticity checks referred to the fraud unit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Online Identity Proofing (IAL2) | 0 (must be unexpired) | yes | 0 | yes |
| Video Trusted Referee Session | 0 (must be unexpired) | yes | 1 | yes |
| In-Person Proofing — American Job Center | 12 | yes | 1 | yes |
| In-Person Proofing — USPS Retail Location | 0 (must be unexpired) | yes | 0 | yes |
| Documentary Verification by Mail | 0 (must be unexpired) | yes | 2 | yes |
| Identity Theft Victim Re-Verification | 12 | yes | 1 | yes |

## Examiner notes

- The grace period for an expired primary document is counted in calendar months from its expiration date; only the American Job Center and identity theft re-verification pathways allow one, of 12 months.
- A permanent resident card is accepted as a primary document on every pathway except Online Identity Proofing (IAL2); a military ID is accepted on the four pathways listed together in section B.
- DD Form 214 and the federal SF-50 are accepted as secondary documents on the American Job Center and mail pathways but not on Identity Theft Victim Re-Verification.
- A resubmission limit of 0 means a rejected document of that role may not be resubmitted on the case.
